CVE-2026-116784.title: FreeSWITCH: Out-of-bounds read in RTCP NACK feedback parsing
CVE-2026-116784.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, process_rtcp_report() used an RTPFB NACK packet's declared RTCP header length as its feedback-entry loop bound instead of the datagram length already validated by the caller. A short packet with an oversized declaration could drive reads far beyond the fixed 16 KiB receive buffer. Any peer able to send RTCP to an active video call can reach the flaw, including calls where remote SDP enables video RTCP even though the SIP profile has no explicit RTCP interval configured. The out-of-bounds read can crash FreeSWITCH and terminate every active call, but supplies no write primitive and does not echo the read values to the sender. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

CVE-2026-126196.title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server read-only mode can be bypassed by SQL statement smuggling through query_database
CVE-2026-126196.description: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. CVE-2026-128086.title: OpenTelemetry-Go: Eager W3C baggage-property materialization causes bounded memory-allocation amplification
CVE-2026-128086.description: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From version 1.0.0-RC1 until version 1.47.0, baggage.Parse and propagation.Baggage.Extract eagerly materialize every W3C baggage property through parseMember, grow property slices, serialize members, and copy properties into internal/baggage.Item. A valid densely populated baggage header can therefore cause allocation traffic and retained memory disproportionate to its bounded input size. Remote impact requires baggage extraction to be enabled, attacker-controlled input to reach it, and extraction to run before authentication or on a public route; the evidence establishes increased allocation and garbage-collection pressure but not reliable process termination. CVE-2026-62298.title: asn1c: ASAN crash with decode of open types
CVE-2026-62298.description: mouse07410/asn1c is an ASN.1 compiler. Prior to 1.2.5, `OPEN TYPE` decoding can dereference an unallocated member pointer and crash the consuming program. `OPEN_TYPE_aper_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_aper.c`, `OPEN_TYPE_ber_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_ber.c`, `OPEN_TYPE_oer_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_oer.c`, and `OPEN_TYPE_uper_get` in `OPEN_TYPE_uper.c` share the pattern: a conditional null check on `*memb_ptr2` resets presence only when the member exists, but execution then unconditionally computes an inner value from that pointer and a member offset. CVE-2026-63583.title: XML injection in ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3
CVE-2026-63583.description:
ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3 interpolates caller-supplied lifecycle rule fields (the rule id, filter prefix, tag key and value, storage class, and noncurrent-version count) directly into the PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration XML body without escaping XML metacharacters. An application that populates any of these fields from untrusted input (for example a tenant-supplied object tag) lets an attacker break out of the surrounding element and inject arbitrary XML into the request, including an entirely new lifecycle action such as a delete-after-one-day expiration that destroys the bucket's objects. The public entry point ExAws.S3.put_bucket_lifecycle/2 flows directly into this builder.

This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.3.0 before 2.6.0.

CVE-2026-80302.title: Avast sandbox escape via arbitrary file write in virtualized environment
CVE-2026-80302.description:
Insufficient isolation in the Avast sandbox file virtualization layer on Windows allows a local, low-privileged attacker executing inside the sandbox to write arbitrary files outside sandbox containment and execute code on the host.

The sandbox virtualizes file system operations by intercepting write requests to protected system directories. However, the virtualization implementation fails to properly validate write targets in certain edge cases, allowing writes to bypass the virtualization redirection and reach the actual host file system in protected locations.

An attacker can exploit this to overwrite executable files, system libraries, or startup configurations with arbitrary content, leading to code execution with host privileges on subsequent system operations or reboot.

CVE-2026-99708.title: ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes
CVE-2026-99708.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: reject wrapped temporary address preferred lifetimes

ipv6_create_tempaddr() raises a temporary address's preferred lifetime to
regen_advance + age + 1 when the configured lifetime is too short. The
result is stored in a u32, while regen_advance and age are unsigned long.
If the sum wraps or is truncated, the stored lifetime can still be less
than or equal to regen_advance + age.

addrconf_verify_rtnl() then sees the new address as due for regeneration
and creates another one. Temporary addresses are not limited by
max_addresses since commit 4b08a8f1bd8c ("ipv6: remove max_addresses
check from ipv6_create_tempaddr"), so this can cause unbounded address
growth. With dad_transmits set to -1, a baseline kernel reached 2859
loopback addresses in two seconds.

After storing the adjusted lifetime, verify that it is still greater than
regen_advance + age. Reject the new address if the check fails.

On an x86-64 KASAN…
